Evidence

The data behind the atlas

Historical maps establish a baseline. Dated field observations help us test their accuracy and record what has changed.

Published datasets used as sources for Atlas research
DatasetObservation periodDetailUse in the Atlas
Nigeria tree canopy coverAlegbeleye and colleagues2017 / 2020 / 202430 mHistorical canopy estimates across Nigeria. Read the paper.
Global Canopy Height v2WRI and MetaVaries by imageApprox. 1 mCanopy structure and boundaries, with local validation and acquisition dates.
Dynamic WorldGoogle and WRI2015–present10 mPossible land-cover changes to investigate through closer imagery and field checks.
Global Mangrove WatchGlobal Mangrove Watch partnership1985–202530 mMangrove extent and coastal context, reported as a distinct habitat layer.
How canopy and shade will be measured

Canopy cover is the share of a fixed land area covered by the overhead projection of tree crowns. Overlapping crowns count once. Each estimate needs an imagery date, an independent reference sample and a measure of uncertainty. Comparable imagery and a consistent denominator are required to estimate change.

Pedestrian shade, verified tree survival and mangrove extent have their own measures and evidence dates. Initial urban footprints can be checked against the GHSL Urban Centre Database.

Lagos · Published field research

A closer look at street trees

Adeyemi and Shackleton surveyed forageable street tree resources in 32 sampled wards across 16 local government areas. Their findings offer a field reference for the city.
